summary: Preterit actor forms include čəlle/čəlla/čərre; keep the source spellings. The different patient types (clothes, paper, ear, belly) retain physical tearing under 1.

The Detransitive contrasts physical tearing with no expressed actor (shirt or torn spot) against actor-caused tearing. PrS 8/14 supplies both gmičər in the hypothetical consequence and Kmičər in the actual comparison.

The single existing sense 2 occurrence at 62/293 has an affected personal suffix -li and an overt expression of weariness after a prolonged dispute. It supports distress/wearing out, but is insufficient to remove the inherited question marks or narrow the gloss to a particular emotion.
Kurdish origin is inherited etymological evidence, not proof of a new light-verb construction. No separate new idiom is established by the body-part combinations.
PrS 15/4 and 53/1 closely or exactly match existing examples with different PrS references; they are not reprinted as independent examples.
Confirm the gender/default agreement and actual-result reading of gmičər/Kmičər in PrS 8/14 against feminine čiro and qaməste in PrS 8/11.
Check PrS numbering for the clothes-tearing quotations: supplied 15/4 and 53/1 versus inherited 30/14,145/16 and 149/19.
Does čəlluxli at 62/293 mean wearing someone out, driving someone to despair, or another degree of distress? Keep the inherited uncertain gloss pending further evidence.
Tearing open bellies is literal physical tearing with a body-part object; it does not require a separate cutting sense. The ear example already establishes body-part patients.
